builder_plan.scenario: A self-hosted assistant is too expensive because its model uses most of the GPU memory.
builder_plan.change: Try the paper's supported lower-precision weights on a copy of your serving setup.
builder_plan.baseline: The same model at its original precision, on the same GPU.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Peak memory, task pass rate, latency, and total serving cost at the same context and load.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: FourSight: Stable FP4 RL Post-Training via Sequence Filtering and Sparse Channel Compensation
summary: FourSight replaces naive NVFP4 W4A4 quantization in RL post-training by combining TIM-aware sequence filtering to exclude drifted trajectories with sparse precision compensation that keeps only high-variance activation channels in BF16, plus a fused SpliceGEMM kernel. The method adds kernel complexity and requires engine-specific implementation for the fused prefill/decode datapaths, with step time within 2.3% of baseline FP4. Severely mismatched tail tokens may still evade filtering if the outlier concentration assumption does not hold for a given model or task, and the approach targets models at scales (up to 120B) that exceed the reader's 24 GB GPU capacity.
rationale: The technique addresses FP4 RL post-training stability at scales up to 120B parameters, requiring fused kernel engineering and model sizes beyond a single 24 GB GPU, making it relevant to monitor but not directly adoptable without significant infrastructure changes.
technique: FP4 RL post-training with sequence filtering and sparse channel compensation

The method adds kernel complexity and requires engine-specific implementation for the fused prefill/decode datapaths, with step time within 2.3% of baseline FP4. Improves step-to-accuracy by 1.76-2.60x while staying within 2.3% of FP4 step time and sustaining near-BF16 accuracy across models up to 120B scale.
